rounds.text: JNK India Ltd carries an expensive valuation paired with severe institutional desertion and alarming balance sheet strains. The stock trades at a demanding P/E of 40.7x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 22.48x, both sitting notably above sector benchmarks [E11]. This premium pricing offers virtually zero margin of safety at a razor-thin 0.3%, leaving the share price highly vulnerable given its historical annualised volatility of 56.2% and a brutal maximum drawdown of -76.9% [E40, E47, E48]. Furthermore, smart money is fleeing aggressively, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings tumbling from 3.50% to 0.94% and domestic institutions cutting their stake from 18.53% to 10.91%, driving a negative institutional money flow signal [E36, E37, E38]. Operational quality also shows major cracks, as cash conversion sits at a dismal 0.31x with operating cash flow covering only half of operating profit, pointing directly to potential receivables or accrual issues [E28, E31]. Compounding these fundamental risks, borrowings have surged significantly to Rs 58 Cr from just Rs 19 Cr a year earlier [E33], and operating margins have eroded by 5 percentage points over three years [E24]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales and profit growth alongside high relative strength [E16, E19, E45].
